title: Law firms give lawyers time off billing grind to test-drive AI
key_facts: Reuters (Sara Merken and David Thomas) reports that law firm Ropes & Gray said its 1,000-plus associates and counsel can now count up to 100 hours of AI experimenting and training toward their annual billing requirements.
The move is part of a firmwide AI training initiative; the rest of the sentence was cut off in the excerpt.
quote_evidence: As Ropes & Gray ramps up its use of AI, the law firm said its 1,000-plus associates and counsel can now count up to 100 hours of AI experimenting and training toward their annual billing requirements.
why_it_matters_hint: Law firms are paying for AI learning time by crediting it against lawyers' billable-hour targets.
notes: Reuters page returned 401; TradingView carries only the opening paragraph (meta description) of the Reuters article. The headline says 'law firms' (plural); only the Ropes & Gray detail was visible. Treated as headline plus lede, not a full read.
